name: Alphalete - Local Page Build Session 2026-05-20
body:
> Report · Alphalete · 2026-05-20

Also: `alphalete-trenchless-website\context\site-audit-tracking.docx` (May 27)

# Summary
The session that created most of the programmatic local pages. On May 20 2026 local coverage was expanded to all 44 cities across the target services: **105 new city service pages** were generated, given Yoast SEO, and published. The same session repaired about 2,200 broken internal links across 78 pages and filled 255 missing image metadata fields.

# How the pages were built
1. Pulled a template page's Elementor data over SSH with wp-cli.
2. Mapped every text-bearing widget (headings, paragraphs, icon boxes, FAQ items, JSON-LD, HTML widgets).
3. Wrote 3 copy variants per shared section and 3 FAQ pools, with the city woven into hero, intro, area headings and one FAQ.
4. A Node.js generator built each city's Elementor JSON with a deterministic variant mix.
5. Uploaded via SCP and created pages with `wp eval-file` (parent, author, Yoast meta, cache flush), then spot-checked.

# Templates used
- Drain cleaning: Buffalo Creek (ID 9381), 21 pages created, parent 5543 (`/service-areas/`).
- Commercial trenchless pipelining: Black Forest (ID 12379), 43 pages, parent 5381 (`/services/`), with rebuilt per-page FAQ schema and an "Areas We Also Serve" widget.
- Further services are covered in the full report.

# May 27 coverage audit (site-audit-tracking.docx)
- 44 cities defined in `alphalete_city_coords()` in the mu-plugin. Across trenchless, drain and hydro: 132 expected, 131 published.
- Only gap: `drain-cleaning-services-in-manitou-springs` (ID 12389) left as a draft.
- Recommended next: a meta-completeness sweep (after an Apr 22 title bleed-through), a thin-content scan under about 400 words, and snapshots for future comparison. Full DB backup noted at `~/alphalete-pre-seo-backup.sql`.

# Why it matters now
These variant-built pages are the "about 237 mostly programmatic pages" that later audits flagged as near-duplicates (95% identical in the Jul 22 baseline) and the root of the June to August indexing problems.
